bbva.intro: BBVA shows solid progress in structuring its 'Net Zero' roadmap between 2024 and 2025, evidenced by the expansion of scope towards key sectors such as Aluminium and cargo Aviation. However, the bank faces transparency challenges arising from methodological restatements in Oil & Gas and an alarming deviation in meeting short-term targets in its Steel portfolio.

points.title: Critical setback and lack of transparency in Steel
points.body: It is essential to focus on the 12% increase in the Steel sector's physical intensity reported in 2025 versus the previous year. This sharp rise is presented without any contextual or macroeconomic explanation in the report, undermining the credibility of the 2030 target for this heavy portfolio.

points.title: Break in the historical series in Oil & Gas due to inclusion of 'midstream'
points.body: The change to the base-year absolute emissions of the Oil & Gas portfolio (an increase of 0.6 MtCO2e) improves completeness but breaks the comparability of the progress reported in 2024, constituting a methodological risk as the ambition of the final reduction percentage was not clearly reformulated.

points.title: Impossibility of traceability in the Shipping portfolio
points.body: The adoption of the Poseidon Principles v4 as the governing framework in the 2025 report versus the previous 2024 model hinders continuous transition-risk tracking for maritime assets, requiring a bridge baseline to be established so that investors can measure shipowners' real improvement.

points.title: Strengthening by bringing forward commitments in Coal
points.body: The decision to bring forward by two years (from 2040 to 2038) the target for eliminating global thermal-coal exposure, as certified in the 2025 report's strategic update, is a highly positive signal for the market.

santander.intro:
As a final conclusion of this comparative analysis, an evolution towards flexibility and operational pragmatism is observed, at the expense of the rigidity of the initial commitments.
Banco Santander's overall evolution shows a pragmatic refocusing of its decarbonization strategy, moving away from fixed, absolute targets towards flexible intensity ranges. This adjustment, which the bank attributes to the need to reflect the real pace of transition and the dependence on public policy, mainly affects the comparability of its commitments in the most polluting sectors and denotes a loosening of the climate scenarios previously adopted.

points.title: Setback in Oil & Gas ambition
points.body:
The absolute-emissions target is removed and Scope 3 is excluded from the alignment target, shifting to a monitoring-only metric (Primary Energy Index).
Scope 3 emissions (those generated by the use of the products sold by oil companies) typically account for more than 80–90% of the sector's total impact. By moving these emissions to a "monitoring index" (Primary Energy Index) instead of a portfolio-linked reduction target, the direct pressure on clients' carbon imbalance decreases. The bank justifies this by stating that clients have "greater operational control" over their Scopes 1 and 2.

points.title: Methodological shift towards target ranges
points.body: The bank has systemically replaced its emission targets set as a strict value (whether absolute or intensity) with flexible intensity ranges (in Power, Steel, Automotive), arguing the need to absorb the different international transition speeds.

points.title: Massive update of base years
points.body:
The base years of most CIB sectors have been reset from 2019 to 2023, hindering the traceability of long-term historical progress.
Changing the base year makes it harder to compare historical progress. If a bank reduces emissions between 2019 and 2023 but then "resets" the counter in 2023, the long-term trajectory becomes fragmented. The bank argues that this change seeks to use more recent and accurate data to reflect the current composition of its portfolio.

points.title: Reclassification of hard-to-abate sectors
points.body:
The bank has given up maintaining a decarbonization target for aviation, moving it to "monitoring" citing a lack of control over the sector's levers.
This represents a loosening of the climate commitment in a hard-to-abate sector. The bank explains that, given the current size of its exposure (EUR 0.53 billion) and the total dependence on external technologies such as sustainable fuel (SAF), it does not consider it feasible to maintain a binding alignment target at this time.

points.title: Alteration of the baseline climate scenario
points.body: The institution has abandoned the exclusivity of the IEA Net Zero 2050 scenario, incorporating the less restrictive Announced Pledges Scenario (APS) into the definition of all its new sectoral target ranges.

sabadell.intro: Banco Sabadell shows overall progress in its decarbonization strategy, achieving notable intensity reductions in key sectors. When the institution's explanations are taken into account, it becomes clear that the volatility in the monitoring indicators largely reflects the high concentration of certain portfolios and temporary mismatches in the availability of client data.

points.title: Exceptional drop in the power sector
points.body: Physical intensity has plunged to 40 Kg CO2e/MWh, beating the lower bound of the target range (45–85) ahead of schedule thanks to the weight of renewable project finance.

points.title: Justified spike in oil and gas
points.body: The rise in emissions to 5,277 Kt CO2e (versus the previous 4,820 Kt CO2e) underscores the sensitivity of the absolute footprint to new one-off commercial-credit drawdowns.

points.title: Impact of concentration in aluminium and coal
points.body: The atypical rise in aluminium intensity (+9.8%) and the spike in coal exposure (from EUR 0.1m to EUR 1.7m) show that, in small or highly concentrated portfolios, working-capital lines or mix changes significantly distort the trend towards 2030.

points.title: Data lag in Shipping
points.body: The worsening of the Alignment Delta to +28% highlights the current challenges in ESG data quality, forcing the bank to use one-year lags (2023 data to estimate 2024).

points.title: Marked progress in automotive
points.body: The abrupt improvement to 183 gCO2e/vkm validates the portfolio-reallocation strategy towards automotive groups with more aggressive transition plans.

caixabank.intro: CaixaBank's overall evolution towards decarbonization shows accelerated progress in the energy sectors (Power and Oil & Gas), far exceeding the 2030 targets, but presents stagnation and even severe setbacks in sectors linked to external regulatory changes such as Automotive, or with proxy-data problems such as Commercial Real Estate. Methodologically, the baseline is consistent, although occasional numerical discrepancies surface in the historical recalculation of certain years.

points.title: Severe worsening and discrepancy in the Automotive sector
points.body: An alarming increase has been observed in the automotive sector's emissions intensity in 2025 (163.9 gCO2/vkm), exceeding even the base-year level (154 gCO2/vkm) due to regulatory loosening in Europe, compounded by a retroactive alteration of the 2023 figure with no further justification in the latest report.

points.title: Early achievement of 2030 targets
points.body: The power-generation and oil-and-gas portfolios have experienced drastic falls in their absolute metrics and physical intensities, with both standing in 2025 below the final target the bank had set out to reach within five years.

points.title: Setback in Commercial Real Estate driven by proxies
points.body: The bank reports an increase to 21 kgCO2e/m2 in its commercial real estate portfolio in 2025 that exceeds the original starting point (20.5 kgCO2e/m2), driven not by a real emissions increase but by a methodological adjustment in the estimation of proxy data given the lack of actual certificates.

points.title: Silent adjustment of historical data in Power
points.body: In cross-checking the reports, a retroactive change has been identified in the intensity figure for financial year 2022 for the power sector, moving from the 116 kgCO2e/MWh reported in 2024 to 118 kgCO2e/MWh in 2025, suggesting internal recalculations that affect the public traceability of the metric.

hsbc.intro: HSBC's evolution in 2025 reflects a deep restructuring of its reporting strategy, prioritizing flexibility through target ranges and the use of updated data. This move improves technical accuracy but makes it harder to directly trace the bank's historical commitments.

points.title: Methodological changes affecting comparability
points.body: All fixed reduction targets have been replaced with "target ranges," allowing the bank to absorb deviations from the macroeconomic scenario.

points.title: Cross-sector update of climate scenarios
points.body: The exclusive use of the IEA NZE 2021 scenario has been abandoned in favour of an approach based on the IEA NZE and APS 2024 scenarios.

points.title: Base-year changes
points.body: Baselines have been updated from 2019 to 2023 in five of the seven key sectors, resetting the accumulated-progress counter.

points.title: Sectors removed
points.body: The aluminium sector has been removed from the alignment-target framework due to its limited weight on the balance sheet.

points.title: Metric change in Aviation
points.body: The shift from passenger-kilometres (RPK) to revenue tonne-kilometres (RTK) represents a fundamental adjustment to comprehensively cover airlines that carry cargo.

barclays.intro: The bank's overall evolution in its decarbonization strategy shows mixed results, alternating refinements to its measurement methodologies with real setbacks in key sectors of its portfolio. While adjustments aimed at more accurately reflecting baselines and alignment with stricter climate scenarios are evident, the rise in absolute emissions in heavy industry and fossil-fuel sectors represents a direct challenge to its path to net zero.

points.title: Methodological adjustment in real estate and power portfolios
points.body: Baseline intensities have been recalculated in the Power, Commercial Real Estate and Residential Real Estate sectors, directly affecting the historical comparability of the reported data.

points.title: Consolidation of climate scenarios
points.body: Removal of the IEA SDS reference scenario for the Power sector, now relying exclusively on the more ambitious IEA NZE 2050 scenario.

points.title: Extreme volatility in the cement industry
points.body: Sharp year-on-year increase in the sector's absolute financed emissions, which practically double, moving from 0.8 MtCO2e to 1.5 MtCO2e.

points.title: Deterioration in the energy transition
points.body: Clear worsening in the Oil & Gas (Upstream Energy) pathway, where the cumulative reduction falls from -45% to -41% due to a rise in the volume of absolute emissions.

natwest.intro: NatWest has shown an evolution towards greater technical sophistication and financial ambition, integrating climate risks more structurally into its risk policies through the creation of unified sectoral frameworks. However, the recurring change in measurement methodologies and the adoption of stricter reference scenarios between 2024 and 2025 make it harder to linearly trace real progress in critical sectors such as power and steel.

points.title: Abandonment of external validation
points.body: The bank has withdrawn its SBTi-validated targets, opting for a framework of its own design not validated by that initiative.

points.title: Leap in financial ambition
points.body: The climate and transition financing target has doubled, moving from a £100 billion commitment for 2025 to a new £200 billion target by the end of 2030.

points.title: Lack of comparability in the Power sector
points.body: The shift towards "portfolio-level activity-based targets" in power generation has invalidated a direct comparison with previous years' data.

points.title: Formalization of the Oil & Gas target
points.body: The bank has moved from qualitative monitoring to setting a quantitative physical-intensity reduction target of 13% for 2030, also setting 2023 as the new reference base year.

points.title: Tightening of industrial scenarios
points.body: The alignment pathway for the steel sector has become more demanding by migrating from the IEA SDS scenario to IEA Net Zero Emissions (NZE) 2050, contributing to a fall in reported physical intensity from 1.48 tCO2e/t to 1.41 tCO2e/t.

stanchart.intro: Standard Chartered's decarbonization pathway has evolved from the launch of its roadmap in 2021, initially focused on key sectors such as power and transport, to completing in 2024–2025 the setting of science-based targets for all 12 NZBA sectors with the addition of Agriculture. In 2025, the bank completed its Scope 1 and 2 operational neutrality commitment and has begun refining its financed-emissions metrics, incorporating methane intensities and adjusting Scope 3 methodologies to better reflect the reality of its clients in transition.

points.title: Achievement of Net Zero Operational Emissions
points.body: The 2025 report confirms that the bank reached its net-zero target for Scopes 1 and 2 in 2025, following a 96% reduction from the 2018 baseline.

points.title: New Facilitated Emissions Target
points.body: Addition in the 2025 report of the first target for facilitated emissions (capital markets), focused on Oil & Gas with a 26.9% reduction target for 2030.

points.title: Critical Increase in Aluminium
points.body: The aluminium sector's intensity jumped 105% in the 2025 report due to short-term lending operations to highly intensive primary producers.

points.title: Readjustment of the Agriculture Target
points.body: The 2025 report raises both the baseline and the target temperature range (ITR) of the sector following an update to CDP's external scoring factors.

points.title: Methodological Change in Oil & Gas Scope 3
points.body: The 2025 report restricts the Scope 3 calculation solely to upstream production activities, which has forced restatements of the previous year's data.

lloyds.intro: Lloyds Banking Group demonstrates methodological maturity in its climate-transition strategy, deepening its systemic approach and nature (biodiversity) integration. Substantial progress is evident, with a 36% fall in absolute financed emissions and a swift, proactive recalibration of its heaviest portfolios to strictly align with new UK national policies.

points.title: Methodological transition to the Seventh Carbon Budget
points.body: The bank updated its financed-emissions target-setting models for the residential mortgages, commercial real estate, agriculture, passenger transport and automotive portfolios in the 2025 report to align with the new requirements of the CCC's Seventh Carbon Budget, changing the technical baseline underpinned by the Sixth Budget during 2024.

points.title: Tightening of sustainable-automotive financing criteria
points.body: From January 2025, the group tightened the eligibility criteria for its sustainable-vehicle financing target, excluding plug-in hybrid vehicles to focus solely on pure electrics, representing a material change of scope versus that reported in the 2024 report.

points.title: Pioneering integration of TNFD LEAP pilots
points.body: To strengthen the analysis of nature-related risks and dependencies (biodiversity), the bank completed in 2025 a pilot proof-of-concept aligned with the TNFD LEAP framework focused on its Real Estate and Agricultural lending portfolios, an analytical advance not present in the 2024 report's planning.

points.title: 36% fall in absolute financed emissions and record green mortgages
points.body: The group reported a highly positive year-on-year performance, reducing its consolidated financed emissions to 18.6 MtCO2e (a 36% fall versus 2018) per the 2025 report, driven by extraordinary growth in its sustainable-mortgage portfolio (EPC A and B) which scaled to £18.5 billion in 2025, up from £11.4 billion accumulated the previous year.

points.title: Definitive timeline for exiting corporate thermal coal
points.body: In a significant reinforcement of its exclusion commitments, the 2025 report's roadmap formally announced the target of fully exiting any entity operating thermal-coal facilities by 2030, successfully building on the cessation of direct financing for UK coal power already achieved at the end of 2023.

ing.intro: Across the years assessed, ING shows a favourable and highly active evolution towards decarbonizing its portfolios, achieving consistent methodological reductions in emissions intensity in the heaviest sectors of its balance sheet (such as Power and real estate). However, the institution continues to face the difficult reality of hard-to-abate sectors (aviation, automotive and cement), where emissions intensity has seen slight upticks linked to variations in credit drawdowns and the limited availability of technological alternatives at scale.

points.title: SBTi validation of targets
points.body: A corporate turning point, reported in 2025, has been the validation of the bank's climate targets (Terra approach) by the Science Based Targets initiative (SBTi), aligned with a 1.5°C scenario.

points.title: Substantial change of scope in Upstream Oil & Gas
points.body: To align with the requirements of the SBTi-validated methodological framework, the bank has transitioned from setting its targets and measuring its exposures based on outstanding balances to relying strictly on committed loan limits.

points.title: Methodological update in Commercial Real Estate
points.body: A material restatement of emissions has been implemented, replacing "Well-to-Wheel" emission factors with "Tank-to-Wheel" ones, which has retrospectively altered its baseline and changed the actual measurement of its trajectory.

points.title: Change in the Steel sector's measurement metric
points.body: The bank has replaced its previous "Alignment score" with a stricter percentage-deviation system based on the latest updates to the Sustainable STEEL Principles standard.

points.title: New sectors for Terra
points.body: The bank's climate-tracking methodology is beginning to branch out into complex areas of the real economy, formally announcing the addition and active development of transition plans for aluminium and agriculture (dairy).

socgen.intro: Societe Generale shows notable progress in its decarbonization pathway, achieving its 2030 targets early in the Power and Shipping sectors. However, significant challenges are observed in hard-to-abate sectors such as steel, where the portfolio has lost its alignment status, along with methodological adjustments in Oil & Gas and Aluminium driven by changes of data provider to refine measurement.

points.title: Early achievement of targets in Power and Shipping
points.body: The bank has comfortably beaten its 2030 targets in two key sectors: in Power, emissions intensity fell to 85 gCO2/kWh (versus the 125 gCO2/kWh target), and in Shipping the alignment score improved to +7.9% (beating the +15% target).

points.title: Misalignment in the Steel sector
points.body: The steel portfolio's alignment score has worsened, moving from an aligned level of -0.61 to a non-aligned level of +0.16. The bank attributes this deviation to the fact that its portfolio's decarbonization depends on the progress of green-steel projects, whose European context is currently less favourable.

points.title: Methodological and baseline adjustments in Oil & Gas and Aluminium
points.body: Methodological changes have occurred due to the rotation of data providers and corrections to client data. This has caused the Oil & Gas absolute-emissions baseline to be adjusted downward (from 29.6 to 24.8 MtCO2eq) and the reported intensity in Aluminium to show an apparent increase (from 6.9 to 7.6 tCO2/t) that does not reflect a real deterioration of the portfolio but rather a change in measurement.

points.title: Tightening of the Thermal Coal sectoral policy
points.body: In March 2025, the bank updated its sectoral policy for thermal coal, broadening the definition of "coal developers" and tightening exclusion thresholds for power producers that have not made a public phase-down commitment, while also clarifying exemptions for energy-transition operations.

deutsche.intro: Deutsche Bank has shown solid progress in reducing physical intensities across most of its target sectors, such as Power and Automotive. However, it faces pressures and upward volatility in specific sectors such as Coal and Cement. Changes in data-consolidation criteria and the removal of contingent commitments have notably altered the corporate financed-emissions ledger.

points.title: Exclusion of contingent commitments and restructuring of emissions
points.body: In the 2025 report, the bank introduced a high-impact structural methodological change by fully excluding the commitment to issue contingents from the corporate portfolio's boundary. This optimization retroactively changed the data for year-end 2024, reducing reported financed emissions by 5.8 MtCO2e/y for Scopes 1 and 2, and by a severe 81.4 MtCO2e/y for Scope 3.

points.title: Increase in financed emissions in the Coal sector
points.body: Despite global fossil-fuel reduction commitments, absolute Scope 3 financed emissions in coal mining rose from 4.6 MtCO2/y to 5.3 MtCO2/y between the two reports. This 16% setback is attributed to short-term financing lending activity directed at a single client.

points.title: Downward methodological recalibration of the Power baseline
points.body: The bank applied a deep reconfiguration in the power sector by more precisely integrating small generating entities and subtracting contingent commitments. As a direct result, the 2021 base-year physical intensity was adjusted downward from 396 kgCO2e/MWh to 367 kgCO2e/MWh, and the interim target set for 2030 became stricter, falling from 124 kgCO2e/MWh to 114 kgCO2e/MWh.

points.title: Expansion of Scope 3 and inclusion of facilitated emissions
points.body: In order to increase transparency in its capital-markets activities, Deutsche Bank expanded in its 2025 report the category-15 metrics by incorporating facilitated emissions under the December 2023 standard PCAF methodology. To mitigate the volatility inherent to transaction-structuring volume, the bank began disclosing 5-year moving averages, reporting total facilitated emissions of 8.5 MtCO2/y (Scope 1 and 2) and 118.1 MtCO2/y (Scope 3) for 2024.

points.title: Persistence of deviations in the Cement sector
points.body: The cement sector continues to stand out as a critical area with serious technological mitigation challenges. Reported physical intensities stood at 749 kgCO2e/t of cement in the 2025 report, representing a persistent 11% upward deviation versus the recalculated 2022 baseline values (678 kgCO2e/t), due to the portfolio's small size, which limits active rebalancing management.

unicredit.intro: UniCredit shows a positive consolidation in integrating its climate commitments into the group's risk-management processes and financial planning. The bank has achieved consistent reductions in the intensity and emissions levels of its active portfolio, positioning itself below the interim targets set for 2030 in several key sectors.

points.title: Inclusion of corporate bonds and baseline recalculation
points.body: In the 2025 report, UniCredit implemented a highly significant methodological change by incorporating bond securities into the measurement scope for the Power Generation and Oil & Gas sectors. This caused a retroactive recalculation of the 2021 baselines, altering previous comparative values versus those reported in the 2024 report.

points.title: Mandatory transparency via EPC in the real estate sector
points.body: With the aim of improving quality and reducing the high volume of estimated data in its Real Estate portfolios, UniCredit announced in its 2025 report that collecting actual Energy Performance Certificates (EPC) is now mandatory for new Commercial and Residential Real Estate transactions, representing a step forward in transparency versus the 2024 report.

points.title: Future commitments and policy development for Agriculture
points.body: UniCredit substantially changed its approach to the agriculture sector in the 2025 report by detailing concrete plans to structure internal sustainable-practice guidelines, an employee training programme focused on the sector for 2026, and the creation of a formal sectoral policy, going beyond the initial passive-monitoring stance in the 2024 report.

intesa.intro: The bank's evolution in its decarbonization process during 2024 and 2025 shows a steady effort to refine its methodologies and align with more up-to-date scenarios, notably including the recent validation of its targets by SBTi. A general downward trend is observed in most physical intensities and absolute emissions, strongly conditioned by readjustments in portfolio exposure volume.

points.title: Widespread renewal of reference scenarios
points.body: The bank systematically updated the International Energy Agency's benchmarks (from the 2023/2024 versions to 2025) for the Power, Oil & Gas, Cement, Steel and Automotive sectors.

points.title: Achievement of the coal phase-out
points.body: In 2025, the bank achieved its target of zero exposure to coal-mining counterparties (keeping only a residual doubtful amount), bringing financed emissions from 0.1 Mt CO2e to 0.0 Mt CO2e.

points.title: Sharp reduction in the aluminium sector
points.body: Physical intensity fell sharply from 4.38 tCO2e/t in 2024 to 3.03 tCO2e/t in 2025, while absolute emissions moved from 0.4 to 0.1 Mt CO2e, driven by a notable halving of the sector's financial exposure.

points.title: Upward volatility in steel intensity and agricultural emissions
points.body: Despite portfolio amounts remaining stable, iron and steel's physical intensity rose from 0.82 to 0.90 tCO2/t, while absolute agriculture emissions rose from 0.7 to 0.9 Mt CO2e.

points.title: Innovation in steel-sector metrics
points.body: A novel dedicated-financing approach was introduced in 2025 for the steel sector, isolating and accounting differently for specific technology-transition transactions versus general corporate lending.

nordea.intro: Nordea shows continued progress in its net-zero decarbonization strategy, achieving real reductions in key sectors such as Power, Oil & Gas and Shipping. However, the period analyzed stands out for a thorough methodological and data-quality review that has triggered massive baseline recalculations across multiple portfolios, redefining starting points and making direct comparability of intensity metrics against the previous year harder.

points.title: Methodological recalculation in Agriculture
points.body: The baseline adjustment drastically lowers the initial metric from 758 tCO2e/EURm to 363 tCO2e/EURm, turning the sector's trajectory from a continued reduction into a slight 1.4% increase.

points.title: Sharp fall in Oil & Gas
points.body: Actual absolute emissions have plunged to 0.01 MtCO2e from the previous 0.7 MtCO2e, consolidating an impressive 99.6% reduction through the systematic exit of clients and portfolio rebalancing.

points.title: Downward correction in Residential Real Estate
points.body: The 2019 baseline intensity was significantly adjusted from 17.4 kgCO2e/m2 to 12.2 kgCO2e/m2 as a direct consequence of improvements in data sources and EPC certificates.

points.title: Strong non-organic fall in Commercial Real Estate
points.body: Reported emissions intensity fell drastically from 28 kgCO2e/m2 to 13 kgCO2e/m2, achieving substantial improvements in the metric thanks to updated EPC data, despite a real increase in credit exposure.

points.title: Accelerated fall in Power
points.body: The sector's absolute emissions fell by more than half, from 797,501 tCO2e to 361,603 tCO2e, in a context where credit-portfolio volume experienced clear growth.
